paul-gerard.text: Gerard's campaign says he is running "to restore transparency, fiscal stability, and trust — so every decision the district makes starts with what's best for students."

source.title: Paul Gerard for Burbank Board of Education — Area Three (campaign site)

paul-gerard.text: Pledges to work with district leadership to address BUSD's "Lack of Going Concern" designation by restructuring finances, strengthening internal controls and restoring multi-year budget discipline; says "State takeover is not an acceptable outcome."

source.title: Paul Gerard for Burbank Board of Education — Area Three (campaign site)

paul-gerard.text: Pledges to restore board adherence to the Brown Act: "no more closed-door decisions the public is kept from seeing, and no more retroactive edits to public meeting records."

source.title: Paul Gerard for Burbank Board of Education — Area Three (campaign site)

paul-gerard.text: Pledges to face declining enrollment while keeping educational programs, school facilities and staff compensation "competitive with the best districts in the state."

source.title: Paul Gerard for Burbank Board of Education — Area Three (campaign site)

paul-gerard.text: Wrote that the board "has spent two years managing its image rather than managing its crisis," citing two FCMAT reviews flagging the same internal-control and deficit-projection failures.

source.title: Paul Gerard for Burbank Board of Education — Area Three (campaign site)

paul-gerard.text: "As a trustee of the Burbank Board of Education, I will work to ensure that there are strategic plans that support student achievement by keeping the education of Burbank's youth as the top priority of the district."

source.title: myBurbank: Paul Gerard Files for Burbank Board of Education – District 3 (2026 press release)

rosemary-t-morrison.text: Commits to "helping BUSD continue on the path of fiscal transparency, implementing modern financial practices, and conducting a district-wide audit of how all our money is allocated."

source.title: Rosemary4BurbankSchool — Rosemary Morrison campaign site (Key Priorities)

rosemary-t-morrison.text: Will advocate "investing in competitive educator compensation and strong working conditions so BUSD can recruit and retain exceptional teachers, classified employees, and staff."

source.title: Rosemary4BurbankSchool — Rosemary Morrison campaign site (Key Priorities)

rosemary-t-morrison.text: Lists "supporting our immigrant students and families and keeping our school communities strong and connected" among her student-success priorities.

source.title: Rosemary4BurbankSchool — Rosemary Morrison campaign site (Key Priorities)

rosemary-t-morrison.text: Will advocate "expanding STEM, arts, trades, career technical education, and hands-on learning opportunities" and "protecting classroom programs and resources that directly benefit students."

source.title: Rosemary4BurbankSchool — Rosemary Morrison campaign site (Key Priorities)

rosemary-t-morrison.text: Supports "reasonable, age-appropriate expectations around cellphones and other classroom distractions," saying teachers should be empowered to keep classrooms focused.

source.title: Rosemary4BurbankSchool — Rosemary Morrison campaign site (Key Priorities)

notes: Open seat (formerly Charlene Tabet's; Kelsey Olson's interim appointment ends Dec. 2026). Paul Gerard and Rosemary Morrison have campaign sites with issue positions. No public positions, campaign sites or news coverage beyond filing found for Evren Ozbey, Hai Ho or Dennis M. Connor (checked Burbank Leader, myBurbank archive search, burbankvotes.com). Gerard's site lists individual endorsers (e.g., former Burbank Teachers Association president Diana Abasta), but no organizational endorsements; no BTA endorsement in this race found.
